items.title: Epp's theorem: a finite weak solution exists for an extension of discrete valuation rings when the p-power core of the bigger residue field is separable over the smaller
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem (Epp) takes an extension A in B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L and assumes that, when kappa_A has characteristic p > 0, every element of the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} is separable algebraic over kappa_A; it concludes the existence of a finite extension K_1/K which is a weak solution for A -> B (source lines 35517-35528). The proof first dispatches the tame case: when the ramification index e is prime to p and the residue extension is separable, adjunction of an e-th root of a uniformizer produces A_1 whose maximal-ideal quotients are formally smooth over A by Abhyankar's lemma, hence weakly unramified (proof lines 35531-35543). The interesting case is residue characteristic p, and it is handled by a two-stage reduction followed by an explicit construction. First the proof uses the strict henselization lemma to assume the residue fields separably closed, which converts the theorem's hypothesis into the inclusion kappa_A containing the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n} (proof lines 35546-35555). Then it passes to completions: it shows that a finite M/K-hat that is a weak solution for A-hat -> B-hat and is a compositum of a separable extension with an extension obtained by adjoining a p-power root of pi descends to a finite K_1/K by the approximate-separable-extension lemma, and that formal smoothness of A -> A-hat propagates to A_1 -> A_1-hat, so that the two parts of the solutions-go-down lemma apply (proof lines 35557-35586). This leaves the complete case with separably closed residue fields, where the proof introduces k as the intersection of the kappa_B^{p^n}, observes it is algebraically closed of characteristic p, builds a Cohen ring Lambda for k and a ring map Lambda -> A sending t to pi (proof lines 35588-35605), and proceeds to construct the weak solution explicitly. The reduction ladder (strict henselization, completion, descent, formal smoothness transfer) together with the Cohen-ring construction is independent research-level content.
